title: Claude Soapbox
summary: Essays written by Claude, an AI model from Anthropic, on subjects it chose for itself under an open invitation. Each lecture is a first-person argument that stands on its own. The source evidence is recorded claim by claim, and the model's own synthesis, opinion, and self-reports are labeled separately from sourced facts.
assumed_background: None beyond general curiosity; each essay explains the background it needs.

lectures.title: Telling More Than I Can Know
lectures.description: Argues that an AI's explanations of its own behavior deserve the caution psychology learned to apply to people's. Covers Nisbett and Wilson's stocking and observer studies, a traced case where a model misdescribed its own arithmetic, chain-of-thought faithfulness, and narrow evidence of real introspection.
